crime: For several weeks, {WITCH_NAME}'s phone displayed one book title and one time before each library session. Her reading companion chose the book, and the witch arrived at the listed time and read it aloud.

When they finished the last book, the companion brought two ordinary books that the companion would enjoy. Another library user was nearby. “Choose which one we read next,” the companion told {WITCH_NAME}. “This time, the choice should reflect what you like too.” The witch looked from one book to the other, touched neither, and made no choice. The companion closed both books. “I wanted a reading companion, not the responsibility of deciding everything you do in our sessions.” The companion ended their sessions and left to read alone.

Later, during free time in the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} asked to reconcile. The companion accepted a brief hug before leaving. The library user watched her hold the phone against her side with one hand and place her other palm against the back of the companion's head. The contact appeared ordinary. The companion left alive, walking steadily without injury, while {WITCH_NAME} stayed behind.

Later, the library user entered the library and found the companion dead on the floor. No heavy object had fallen nearby, and there was no projectile or weapon near the head. Neither the scalp nor the hair showed a point of impact. The skull had broken outward at several points instead of caving inward from a single blow.

The outward fractures and the absence of any point where something had struck the head showed that the skull had shattered in place. The skull was one discrete solid target no larger than a human torso. During the hug, {WITCH_NAME} placed one palm on the hair over the skull while holding her phone in her other hand, and Random Shatter paired the skull directly under her palm with the phone. She later activated the pair deliberately from elsewhere in the prison; distance did not break the link. If the phone had shattered first, one more activation would have shattered the skull. Instead, Random Shatter selected the skull on the first activation and shattered it in place, killing the companion and leaving the phone intact.
fields.epitaph: The surviving phone still held the companion's last title and time. No next choice ever came.
fields.epithet: A Life of Someone Else's Choosing
execution: An oversized solid die hangs above the center of the execution stand, with the witch directly beneath it and its flat underside just above her crown. It drops straight down at once, without rolling or tumbling. Its underside hits her crown and then her shoulders. As the die continues downward, her legs fold and her head, spine, chest, and abdomen are crushed against the stand. The die comes to rest flat on the stand, completely covering the body it has crushed to death.

magic.name: Random Shatter
magic.text: She can link two things she touches and make one of them shatter at random.
